- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, especially if history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.33) or neutral (0.00), particularly if recent prices show mean reversion or consolidation.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast if sentiment is mixed or recently negative — model tends to overreact.
- Correct for lagged mean reversion: if true price drops after a forecast peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next period if sentiment remains neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, reduce forecast slope and cap upward revisions.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid overconfidence in early periods — model often overshoots near the start of the forecast window when sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is consistently 0.67+ over last 5 days, cap forecast at 10% below recent high to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment is 0.33–0.67, use smoothing: don’t jump more than 2% from prior forecast unless price action confirms breakout.
